title.en: Tangent-space normal bake and handedness handoff

summary: Bake and transport tangent-space normals with a fixed UV set, tangent convention and handedness sign so mirrored islands and seams do not invert lighting in Three.js.
objective: A beveled test mesh preserves bump direction and seam continuity under a rotating light in Blender and Three.js, including intentionally mirrored UV regions.
intent_signals: bake high poly normals for glTF
example_prompts: Bake this sculpt to a low-poly glTF without inverted normal-map details.
Fix a mirrored UV seam that changes lighting direction in Three.js.
not_for: Replacing geometry where silhouette or parallax must change.
Assuming all normal-map tools use the same Y convention.

principles: A tangent-space normal is meaningful only with the mesh normals, the UV set and the tangent basis used to interpret it. Treat those as one asset contract.

glTF stores a tangent direction plus a handedness sign and derives the bitangent from normal, tangent and that sign. Mirrored UVs therefore need correct vertex splits and signs rather than a global guess.
A green-channel flip is a convention conversion. Apply it once at bake, image preprocessing or runtime normal scale, record where it occurs, and remove compensating flips elsewhere.
Normal maps change shading, not silhouette. Use geometry or displacement when the outline or actual contact surface must carry the detail.
implementation: Finalize low-poly vertex normals, triangulation and the UV set before the approved bake. Keep a cage or ray-distance choice with the source asset so a rebake is reproducible.

In Blender Cycles, bake tangent-space normals using the glTF exporter manual's stated +X, +Y, +Z channel orientation, save the image, mark it Non-Color and connect it through a Tangent Space Normal Map node to Principled Normal.

Export tangents when the pipeline requires the authored basis, or verify that the consumer generates the glTF-recommended MikkTSpace basis from the same positions, normals and normal-map UVs. Do not recompute mesh normals after baking without rebaking.
On Three.js import, first use the GLTFLoader-created material. If a separately loaded map uses the opposite handedness, negate the Y component of normalScale once and document that conversion.

Include a test asset with diagonal embossing, a hard-normal boundary, a UV seam and a mirrored island; rotate a single light or the object so directional inversions cannot hide in a static environment.
observable_checks: Embossed details remain raised rather than becoming dents under light from four directions.
The mirrored island preserves the intended bump direction and does not show a sign-flipped lobe at its boundary.
A seam close-up under grazing light shows only the declared UV/normal discontinuity; changing camera position does not reveal a new tangent seam.
A silhouette comparison confirms that normal-mapped relief does not claim geometric depth or alter contact.

creative_affordances: Deliberately inverted or amplified normals may create a graphic engraved look when named as stylization.
For distant assets, omit fine normal detail and spend texture bandwidth on base-color or roughness variation that survives the shot.
known_limits: Tangent generation and import behavior are software-version dependent; inspect the actual exported attributes and target renderer.
Mirrored UVs can also expose padding and compression seams beyond tangent handedness.
Authored reusable guidance; no bake, export or render was run for this record.

claims.statement: glTF 2.0 defines TANGENT as normalized XYZ plus a W sign for tangent-basis handedness, derives bitangent as cross(normal, tangent.xyz) multiplied by tangent.w, and recommends default MikkTSpace tangent calculation when tangents are absent but a normal texture is used.
claims.scope: glTF 2.0 mesh tangent semantics; exact implementation behavior still depends on the consumer.

source_refs.locator: Geometry > Meshes: attribute semantics and tangent generation; Materials > Additional Textures: normal texture

claims.statement: Blender's glTF exporter manual specifies a Tangent Space Normal Map node, Non-Color image data and +X,+Y,+Z bake orientation for glTF, while Three.js documents that a left-handed normal-map convention can be compensated by negating the Y component of normalScale.
claims.scope: Current Blender export guidance and Three.js MeshStandardMaterial API; this is a convention conversion rather than proof that every asset needs a flip.
